title: How to convert a string column in a pyspark dataframe to List of Dictionaries?
question:
I have the below dataset which is being converted into a PySpark dataframe.

data = [
    {
    "employee_id": 873547690,
    "employee_name":"abc",
    "emp_deptname": "sales",
    "emp_endpoint": "abc@abc01storage",
    "emp_folder": "messages",    
    "emp_address": [
                {
                    "type": "Home",
                    "city": "Delhi",
                    "apartment_number": "H.Number 124, B block, XYZ Towers",
                    "pincode": "123abc"
                },
                {
                    "type": "Postbox",
                    "city": "Delhi",
                    "apartment_number": "Post Office 12A, Sector 22",
                    "pincode": "456xyz"
                }
            ],
    'event_timestamp': '1995-07-16 13:10:43'
        },
]

I have a restriction that says I cannot use the StructType/StructField to define the schema of this data. I can only use the below string type schema definition.

schema = "employee_id long, employee_name string, emp_deptname string, emp_endpoint string, emp_folder string, emp_address string, event_timestamp string"

But now, when the dataframe is created, the emp_address is losing its list of dictionaries structure and is coming out as a big single string as shown in the below screenshot.

printSchema() output as follows:

This is a problem because I need to perform some computations on this field by passing its items and key:value pairs into a method and later flatten out this field into individual records and etc... So, I would really like to have this field as a list of dictionaries.

When I simply cast the field from its row object into a list() it gets blown to pieces per each letter:

How can I convert my string field emp_address into a list of dictionaries without using StructType in my schema?
answer:
you could update the schema string to accept array of structs.

schema_str = """
    employee_id long, 
    employee_name string, 
    emp_deptname string, 
    emp_endpoint string, 
    emp_folder string, 
    emp_address array<struct<type string, city string, apartment_number string, pincode string>>, 
    event_timestamp string
"""

notice the emp_address format i've provided. that's the only change you'll need.

data_sdf = spark.createDataFrame(data_ls, schema_str)

data_sdf.show(truncate=False)

# +-----------+-------------+------------+----------------+----------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+-------------------+
# |employee_id|employee_name|emp_deptname|emp_endpoint    |emp_folder|emp_address                                                                                                     |event_timestamp    |
# +-----------+-------------+------------+----------------+----------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+-------------------+
# |873547690  |abc          |sales       |abc@abc01storage|messages  |[{Home, Delhi, H.Number 124, B block, XYZ Towers, 123abc}, {Postbox, Delhi, Post Office 12A, Sector 22, 456xyz}]|1995-07-16 13:10:43|
# +-----------+-------------+------------+----------------+----------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+-------------------+

data_sdf.printSchema()

#  |-- employee_name: string (nullable = true)
